_note: Internal nodes of a compiled model that are NOT independent unknowns: each entry maps a node
index to the node whose voltage it follows.
WHY IT MATTERS — AND WHY AN ENTRY MUST NOT BE DROPPED TO TIDY THE FILE UP. A model states its
node COUNT but not which of those nodes it actually writes an equation for. A node it never
drives has an identically-zero row, so a simulator that mints an unknown for it is solving an
equation the model did not state: the row is held up by gmin alone, Newton's update in that
direction is noise, and the symptom is a bias ramp that stalls partway and grinds. Measured on a
kit: 279,127 iterations at residual 35.6 before, 5 iterations at 7.6e-12 after.
Nothing about that symptom points at a missing map entry, and circuitRF cannot derive the entry
(see below), so an entry removed here is a slow, silent regression for every fresh import of
that kit. THIS FILE IS THE FALLBACK THAT MAKES A FIRST IMPORT CONVERGE.
OVERRIDING PER KIT: <workspace>/pdk/<kit>/alias-map.json — beside that kit's own
device-provider.json — is searched FIRST, so a file dropped there wins over this one. That is
where an entry for a kit circuitRF has never seen belongs; this file only carries the ones
needed to make a kit work out of the box. Same format either way:
Passed to the worker as its second argument, on EVERY platform — the Windows launcher forwards
its whole command line to the same crf_worker_main the Linux build runs. A model with no entry
anywhere is unaffected: every node stays an ordinary unknown, which is the correct default.
WHY IT IS DATA AND NOT DERIVED. cmd_probe finds WHICH nodes are degenerate structurally, from
identically-zero Jacobian rows, and needs no data at all. What it cannot reveal is WHICH node
each degenerate one follows — that comes from what the model does with the pair. The model's own
get_delay_v(inst, i, j, tau) calls name a pin PAIR and are already recorded (see g_delay), which
is the most promising route to deriving these entries and retiring this file; it has NOT been
verified against a kit, so nothing depends on it yet.
VERIFYING AN ENTRY RATHER THAN GUESSING IT: run the worker and read its probe line. THE TELL IS
'degenerate' — an identically-zero Jacobian ROW — and NOT the ISOLATED/UNDRIVEN suffix beside
it. Measured with no map loaded, the two nodes that need an alias report
ISOLATED, not UNDRIVEN: rows AND columns are exactly zero (symmetric, every other node's row sum
equals its column sum), and the model's own analytic G carries only a 2e-08 gmin-like diagonal
there. An earlier note here said an un-aliased node reports UNDRIVEN and only becomes ISOLATED
once aliased — that is wrong, and following it means looking for a suffix that never appears and
concluding no alias is needed.
Why an ISOLATED node still needs one: nothing reads its voltage, but an unknown is minted for it
anyway, and a row held up by a 2e-08 diagonal makes Newton's update in that direction enormous
and meaningless. Slaving it removes the unknown instead of scaling it.
Which node it follows is not in the probe at all, and not in anything else the model reports —
see the get_delay_v finding above. It comes from what the model does with the pair, so cite the
evidence when adding one.
